item.title: Will Sweden backtrack on worker deportations as media pressure mounts?
item.description: In this week's podcast: a shift in tone on immigration, Sweden reacts to Trump's foreign policy threats, foreigners adapt to Swedish food habits, and why are women in Sweden much more left-wing than men in their voting preferences?

item.title: TELL US: Are you affected by the coming layoffs at Ericsson in Sweden?
item.description: The Swedish tech giant Ericsson this month announced it wanted to lay off 1,200 workers in Sweden, about one in every ten. We want to hear from readers who are affected about what they think of the redundancy programme.

item.title: Which new laws affecting foreigners in Sweden will be published this spring?
item.description: Sweden's government has published its list of bills scheduled for spring. Tighter citizenship rules, ending issuance of permanent residency, and better rules for researchers are all in there. Revoking existing permanent residency permits is not.

item.title: Grammar guide: When to use compound words in Swedish
item.description: Särskrivning, or writing compound words in Swedish incorrectly as two separate words, is a common mistake among Swedish learners (and among Swedes in general, for that matter). But how do you avoid them?

item.title: Ten easy-access cafés and libraries to study or work from in Stockholm
item.description: Whether you are a student looking for a place to study or someone who works remotely and is looking for a new atmosphere, Stockholm caters to a diverse range of preferences and needs.

item.title: Inside Sweden: Is revoking permits too politically toxic for an election year?
item.description: In this week’s Inside Sweden, Nordic Editor Richard Orange looks at whether the government’s proposal to revoke permanent residence permits is too politically risky to push through before the election — and then breaks down the week’s stories.

item.title: Swedish foodie secrets: How to find Sweden's best semla
item.description: Semlor are traditional Swedish cardamom buns filled with whipped cream and almond paste. But what should you look for in a good semla, and what should you avoid?

item.title: Can you lose your Swedish citizenship if you've never lived in Sweden?
item.description: Children of Swedish citizens can be eligible for citizenship by descent, but it's important to know the rules for hanging on to your Swedish citizenship if you've never lived in the country.

item.title: How to buy your own Swedish island
item.description: Ever felt like spending your summers lounging around on your own island? Or have you always wanted to build a James Bond-style supervillain fort in the middle of the Stockholm archipelago?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Orange weather warning in Skåne, man run over by underground train miraculously survives, more soldiers in the Home Guard and other news from Sweden on Monday.
